subject: Post-demo: deployment path clarification & hosted quickstart questions
messages:
From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah@redwoodinference.com>
To: Ethan Shaw <ethan@finly.ai>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus@redwoodinference.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2028-06-18T15:02:00Z
Subject: Post-demo: deployment path clarification & hosted quickstart questions

Thanks again for taking the time today — really appreciated the frank discussion about where Finly is headed. Quick recap of the call and a few follow-ups so we can recommend the right deployment path (hosted vs dedicated vs private):

Summary of what you shared:
- Primary features on day-1: real-time transaction enrichment and user-facing explanations (short LLM responses, <1s p95 target)
- Expected steady-state: ~60k tokens/day, bursts up to 20 QPS during business hours; seasonal spikes could reach 50 QPS for short windows
- Data sensitivity: transactions include PII; must be encrypted in transit and at rest; Finly needs SOC 2 evidence and the option for VPC connectivity for production
- Cost sensitivity: procurement prefers to start with a low-commit approach and evaluate economics after 2–4 weeks of traffic

Questions / Asks for you (so we can size a clear recommendation):
1) Can you confirm peak sustained QPS over 5-minute windows during spikes? (20 vs 50 above)
2) Do you need private VPC for initial pilot, or would a hosted pilot with strict egress controls and contract-level assurances be acceptable?
3) Any strict regional/data residency requirements (we heard US-only)?
4) Who on your side will own the security questionnaire and legal/ procurement path?

What we can offer for next steps:
- Hosted pilot (recommended initial path): 2-week pilot on our hosted API with a sandbox endpoint, per-route rate-limits, and prefix/KV caching enabled. Fastest to get you running and measure unit economics.
- Dedicated or Private: recommended if you require sustained >40 QPS steady-state, strict network isolation, or an on-prem guideline. We can size a dedicated pool and provide a VPC connector for Private deployments, but these take longer to provision (2–6 weeks).

Attached: Redwood hosted quickstart (walkthrough + sample cURLs) and the demo recording. Marcus and Marissa are looped for technical sizing and commercial follow-up.

Propose: If fine, send the short traffic profile (answer Q1–Q3) and I’ll put together a tailored pilot plan. I’ve also added a calendar link here: https://cal.redwoodinference.com/hannah/30min if you want to sync with Marcus (SRE) + Marissa (solutions).

Best,
Hannah

From: Ethan Shaw <ethan@finly.ai>

Subject: Re: Post-demo: deployment path clarification & hosted quickstart questions

Thanks Hannah — good summary and thanks for the clarification call. Quick answers below: 

1) Peak sustained: recent internal load test shows ~35 QPS sustained for ~10 minutes during our synthetic stress tests; real traffic typically hovers 12–18 QPS. We do have marketing-driven spikes (campaign launches) that pushed short bursts to ~45 QPS for ~2–4 minutes historically.
2) For pilot we are open to hosted as long as we get a contract clause for SOC 2 evidence and an option to upgrade to a VPC connector without re-architecting. Procurement prefers starting hosted to validate functionally, then evaluate Dedicated/Private if economics or network needs demand it.
3) Residency: US-only for now.
4) Security & procurement: Elena Vargas is our security lead (cc’d on this thread); procurement will be CC’d once we land technical comfort.

I’ve attached our security questionnaire — not everything is final, but it should give you a sense of controls we’ll need to hit for production.

Two small asks:
- Can you confirm typical p95 latency on our expected request shape (short prompt, 150 tokens output) on hosted?
- What are the default rate-limits on hosted sandbox endpoints and how do we request higher slices?

Thanks,
Ethan

On Mon, 18 Jun 2028 17:45:00 +0000, Ethan Shaw <ethan@finly.ai> wrote:
> Two small asks:
> - Can you confirm typical p95 latency on our expected request shape (short prompt, 150 tokens output) on hosted?
> - What are the default rate-limits on hosted sandbox endpoints and how do we request higher slices?

Thanks for the questionnaire — that helped. A few quick technical notes to set expectations and a recommended pilot config: 

Latency (hosted)
- For short prompts with 150 tokens out, on our default hosted fleet (g5/analog), typical p95 is ~220–450ms depending on batching behavior. For guaranteed <1s p95 you’re comfortably in hosted territory; we’ll tune batching to avoid tail latency during bursts.

Rate limits & slices
- Sandbox default: 20 QPS per endpoint, 600 TPS token-wise (depends on prompt size).
- Requesting higher slices: we provision per-account rate slices for pilots. For a 2-week hosted pilot we can carve a temporary 40 QPS slice with auto-burst to 60 QPS for short windows, subject to scheduling.

When to pick Dedicated/Private
- Dedicated is usually recommended when you need predictable sustained throughput >40 QPS for heavy usage patterns or want reserved GPU capacity (monthly commit).
- Private (VPC/on-prem) is recommended if you require private networking or on-prem air-gapped deployments. Note: Private requires an MSA addendum and provisioning lead time (2–6 weeks depending on network approvals).

Pilot recommendation
- Start with a 2-week hosted pilot: we’ll give a sandbox endpoint with 40 QPS pilot slice, per-route limits, and prefix/KV caching enabled. We’ll also provide a small telemetry dashboard (token-level cost, p95 latency, error rate) so you can measure economics and quality. If steady-state after pilot looks >40 QPS or procurement insists on a VPC, we transition to Dedicated with a VPC connector.

Next technical step: can you share a short sample traffic profile (requests/min with avg prompt length and output tokens) and a list of ~10 representative prompt examples so we can pre-warm caches for the pilot?

—Marcus

2) Redwood to provision: 2-week hosted pilot sandbox (40 QPS slice, short auto-burst to 60 QPS), telemetry dashboard access, and a pre-warm plan for prefix/KV cache.
3) Security: Redwood will provide SOC 2 evidence and a response to the attached questionnaire within 3 business days.
4) Commercial: Marissa will send a short pilot agreement (no long-term commit) with pilot billing terms and an upgrade path to Dedicated/VPC if needed.

Action owners / timeline:
- Finly (Ethan / Elena): share traffic profile + prompts — due 2028-06-23

- Schedule: quick sync to finalize pilot details — propose Wed 2028-06-21 11:00 AM PT. Book here: https://cal.redwoodinference.com/hannah/30min

If that works I’ll kick off the provisioning checklist and loop in our legal for the pilot agreement. Thanks again — excited to get you into a hosted pilot quickly so we can measure economics and performance.
